By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by the petitioner Jagat Singh with respect to the injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.
2. The accident in the present case took place on 31.08.2008, at around 04:00 AM in the morning.
It is the case of the petitioner that he and his other friends were going to Almora, Uttrakhand from Delhi in car registration No. DL-3C-AE-2268.

The driver of the car was driving it rashly, negligently Jagat Singh vs Bimal Kumar on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50054662/
1 and high speed after crossing Moradabad.
The petitioner and others in the car asked him to drive slowly and carefully but he did not listen.

When the car reached near Prakash Tube Factory,
Thakurdwara - Kashipur Road, Uttarakhand, it collied with a stationery truck, which was parked at the opposite side of the road.

sentences.text: He and Ganesh Singh Bisht were injured in that accident.
Ganesh Singh Bisht died in the hospital after 32 days.
The petitioner was taken to L.D. Bhatt, Government Hospital.
He suffered grievous injuries in that accident.
According to the claim petition, he was working with M/s Zenith Roller Ltd and was earning of Rs.13,000/- per month at the time of accident.
A claim of Rs.10,00,000/- as compensation has been filed by the petitioner 3.
The respondent, the owner of the offending car has filed his reply alleging that this petition was filed in 2017, whereas the accident was of 2008.

Due to this delay of around nine years, he did not remember which driver he had employed at the time of accident nor was able to recall the name of the insurance company from which the vehicle was insured.

In a fire in his house in the year 2015,
the articles /documents in his house were destroyed and he had no document relating to the insurance of his vehicle.
His vehicle was stolen in the year 2010 for which he has taken the insurance claim and for that reason also he has no idea about the insurance of this vehicle on the date of accident.

He has further stated that on 01.09.2008, his vehicle collied with a truck and met with an accident on Pushta Road, near Gas Pump, Geeta Colony, Delhi for which DD entry No. 44-A was lodged on 02.09.2009 in police station Geeta Colony therefore it was not possible that his vehicle was involved in accident in Uttarakhand.
He has opposed the claim of the petitioner.
4. Since the respondent could not disclose the driver or the insurance company, there are no other respondents in this case.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 08.11.2017 :-
(i) Whether Mr. Jagat Singh suffered grievous injury in a motor vehicular accident on 31.08.2008 at about 4.00 a.m. on Thakurdwara Kashipur Road (NH-8) near Prakash Tube Factory, Kashipur, Distt. Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand within jurisdiction of PS Kashipur due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. DL 3C AE2268 (car) owned by the respondent?(OPP)
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate of interest and for which period?

(OPP) 
(iv) Relief.
6.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Jagat Singh examined himself as PW-1, Hari Singh as PW-2 and Gopal Singh as PW-3 alleging them as his co-passengers and the eye-witnesses.
He also examined PW-4 Mahesh Upadhyay, Pharmacist, L.D.B.G. Hospital Uttarakhand, who proved the medical records of the petitioner and other injured as Ex.PW4/B.

The petitioner also examined Jagat Singh vs Bimal Kumar on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50054662/
2 PW-5 constable Sushant Chauhan from Kotwali Kashipur Uttarakhand.
As per his evidence, the records till the year 2008 were weeded out in Kotwali Kashipur vide an entry regarding weeding out of record Mark-X.
Therefore, the DD regarding the accident could not be proved through this witness.
7. In his defence, respondent Bimal Kumar examined himself as R1W1.

He also examined R1W2 Head Constable Narender, who proved FIR 260/10 dated 27.11.2010 Ex.R1W2/A with respect to the theft of his vehicle and result of investigation which is mentioned as untrace Ex.R1W2/B.

The respondent also examined V.K. Gupta, Customer Assistant, SBI, Geeta Colony as R1W3 and Head Constable Govind Kumar as R1W4, who proved the DD No. 44A dated 02.09.2008 and DD No. 27A dated 23.12.2015 as Ex.R1W4/A and Ex.R1W4/B regarding the accident of his car in Delhi on the next day and the fire respectively.
8. I have heard Mr. G.S. Bisht, counsel for petitioner and Mr. Love Kumar, counsel for respondent and perused the records.
9. The issues are decided as follows- 10.

The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1: (i) Whether Mr. Jagat Singh suffered grievous injury in a motor vehicular accident on 31.08.2008 at about 4.00 a.m. on Thakurdwara Kashipur Road (NH8) near Prakash Tube Factory,
Kashipur, Distt. Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand within jurisdiction of PS Kashipur due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. DL 3C AE2268 (car) owned by the respondent?(OPP)
11.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
12. Now in this case, the petitioner Jagat Singh is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and proved copy of his Aadhar card Ex.PW1/1,
attested copy of DD No. 17 & 20 dated 31.08.2008 Ex.PW1/2, particulars of vehicle Ex.PW1/3,
treatment record Mark A and salary certificate Mark B.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the car in which they were travelling.
The driver was driving it in a rash and negligent manner and collided with a stationary truck.
Similar is the evidence of Hari Singh and Gopal Singh, who were examined by him as the other occupants of the car.
13. None of these three witnesses were aware of the details of the driver of the car.

In the petition,
none of these persons have been stated to be the occupants of the car.
In fact, in the petition, the name of petitioner and Ganesh Singh Bisht has come on record as the occupants of the car.

3 examination
, the petitioner stated that the car was arranged by deceased Ganesh but he does not know how Ganesh arrange the car.
In cross-examination, a suggestion was given that Ganesh Singh has been mentioned as the person who arranged the car because it could not be verified as he has passed away.
In cross examination the petitioner stated that the number of the car was told to him by the other occupants.
14. Hari Singh and Gopal Singh does not appear to be the occupants of the car from the records.
They were not injured in the accident according to the DD on record nor is there any medical record to this effect.
After the accident, they have not registered any FIR in the present case.
There is only a DD entry regarding the accident, which too in the form of photocopy and not much legible.
On the contrary, this DD entry shows that there were three injured in the accident - Jagat Singh, Ganesh Singh and Rajinder Singh.
The name of the two eye witnesses examined by the petitioner is not there in this DD, or the medical records of the injured after the accident nor in the petition.
Therefore, the evidence of these eye witnesses is doubtful.
Because there is no FIR in the present case or any other complaint against the driver of the car, this fact also goes against the petitioner.
15. Because the driver has not been made a party in these proceedings, the respondent who is the owner of the vehicle has been bereft of any contrary evidence about this accident by the driver.
The accident happened in the night at around 4 AM.
It must be dark at that time and the fact that the truck was parked on the road may have contributed to the accident.

Since no FIR was registered,
therefore there was no investigation on the issue that who was at fault in the accident.
16. The respondent has proved a DD entry on record according to which his car met with an accident in Delhi.
The date of accident in Delhi is the next day of alleged accident of the present case, which appears to be highly improbable.
If the car was damaged in accident in Uttarakhand, it could not have come to Delhi on the very next day and again met with an accident here.

17. The delay in filing this petition has also prejudiced the respondent because by the time the petition was filed, he lost the crucial information and details of the driver and the insurance company.

Had the claim being filed diligently within the next few days or months of the accident,
the insurance company would have been incorporated as the respondent and made liable for compensation.
The record shows that grievous injury suffered by the petitioner were fracture of shaft humerus left compound grade IIIA, debridgement of shoulder with external fixation.
These injuries are not of such nature which would have prevented the petitioner from filing the case on time.
Further, the petitioner has not proved any original medical bills on record.

18. Therefore, on the basis of aforesaid discussion and all the aforesaid factors it is clear that the petitioner is not able to prove that the accident in the present case was the result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car in which he was travelling though it is true that he suffered grievous injuries in the accident as mentioned above.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the respondent and against the petitioner.

19. These issues are decided simultaneously.
Section 166 MV Act is based on the principle of fault liability.
To seek compensation under this section the claimant has to prove that the cause of the accident was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Devki & others- Neutral Citation No. 2016:DHC:1735 dated 29.02.2016 of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it was held that it is well settled that in proceeding arising out of a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act based on fault liability principle, a person cannot be held liable unless he contravenes any of the duties imposed on him by the common law or by the statue.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Devki & others- Neutral Citation No. 2016:DHC:1735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of motor accident, it is imperative that the claimants show by some evidence that the driver of the motor vehicle had been negligent in relation to the said vehicle and thereby had caused an accident resulting in bodily injuries or death or damage to the property so as to be held liable as the principal tort-feasor.
The owner's liability arises out of his failure to discharge a duty cast on him by the law, on principal vicarious liability.
Proof of negligence is necessary before the owner or the insurance company may be held liable for payment of compensation in a motor accident claim case brought under Section 166 MV Act.

Should a claimant find it difficult to prove evidence with regard to negligence, the option to have resort to no fault liability on the structured formula under section 163-A of MV Act is always available to seek just compensation.
20. Section 166 of the MV Act is based on the principle of fault and negligence which has not been proved in this case.

Undisputedly, the petitioners/claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, but in this case the evidence lead is either deficient or doubtful about the involvement of the offending vehicle and more particularly the act of rash and negligent act on its part.
Therefore, the petition under Section 166 of MV Act cannot be allowed.

This could have been a case if pleaded and proved accordingly under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act but remedy for payment of compensation both under section 163A and section 166 being final and independent of each other as statutorily provided, a claimant cannot pursue his remedies thereunder simultaneously.
The claimant must opt/elect to go either for proceeding under section 163A or under section 166 of the Act, but not under both (Oriental insurance Co. Ltd vs Dhanbai Kanji Gandhi, AIR 2011 SC 1138).

entities.text: Oriental insurance Co. Ltd vs Dhanbai Kanji Gandhi, AIR 2011 SC 1138
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Accordingly, this claim petition stands dismissed.
